answer: Cross-epoch behaviour fingerprinting. Each identity's action timing, counterparty overlap, and response latency form a signature compared across epochs; drift beyond a fixed tolerance triggers a penalty that compounds in an umber ledger visible to all peers. Honest agents spiral through small shifts naturally, while a farm of clones cannot synchronize its wander without collapsing to one average profile. The attacker must run distinct behavioural policies per identity, multiplying operational cost per sybil.
